messages.subject: Effect Plots for RQTL2
messages.body_plain:
In the RQTL package we were able to pull out an effect plot for a specific marker (using find.marker and effectplot)

I am interested in doing this in the RQTL2 package with find_marker but, I do not see the equivalent to effectplot for the new package. Is there an equivalent?

If there is no direct equivalent, is there a way to modify the qtl effects plot described in the RQTL2 user manual to only display a region of a chromosome, rather than the entire chromosome?

messages.subject: Re: Effect Plots for RQTL2
messages.body_plain:
I recently added a function plot_pxg() in the qtl2plot <https://github.com/rqtl/qtl2plot> package, which hopefully does what you want.
I've not yet added it to the R/qtl2 user guide <http://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/vignettes/user_guide.html>.

karl

messages.subject: SNP Associations for F2
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

I have another question about the qtl2 package. I want to pull out the SNP associations and eventually the corresponding gene plot. I have a cvs with the MUGA genotypes for each strain in my F2 cross. I modified this cvs to look like the data file used in the user guide DO example but when I attempt to calculate the strain distribution pattern an error reports that there are no polymorphic markers. The only notable difference that I can think of between my file and the example file is that it contains all of the markers from the MUGA data set, rather than a region specific to a marker.

Is there a better way to do this?

Thanks so much!

messages.subject: Re: SNP Associations for F2
messages.body_plain:
The SNP association analysis that we do in the DO doesn't really apply for an F2 between two inbred strains, as there's no collapsing of multiple alleles that needs to occur. The results you get from scan1() are basically everything.

In plot_scan1, you could use type="p" or type="b" to have points plotted, if you want to see the LOD scores at individual markers.

karl
